title: Usage reporting: batched events and quota handling
goal: Report metered usage to the backend in safe, deduplicated batches without ever losing events on crashes or blocking the agent, and turn quota warnings into clear client behaviour.
scope_in: Collector that subscribes (through the internal bus, lane C025, fed by local accounting from lane C029) to hosted-session usage and records events `{id, type: 'agent_minutes'|'tokens_in'|'tokens_out', qty, at, session_id, agent_id?}`; stable `id` per event (monotonic ULID) so retries dedupe server-side.
Durable JSONL spool in the state dir (`usage/spool.jsonl`, mode 0600): at most 10 000 events and 5 MiB; atomic append, truncated-tail recovery.

Batching: flush when 100 events accumulate, every 30 s, on graceful exit and on reconnect; each POST /v1/usage/events carries <= 500 events and <= 1 MiB and one `Idempotency-Key` per batch (stored with the batch until acknowledged); at most 60 requests/min per device.

Outcome handling: 2xx removes the batch; 429 honours `retry_after_s`; 5xx/network keeps the batch and retries with the C051 backoff; 4xx other than 429 drops the batch and logs the code (poison protection) after one retry for 409 `idempotency_conflict` with a new key only if the body changed.

Quota handling: consume `sys.notice usage_warning {pct, resets_at}` and `quota_reached {resets_at}` plus `quota_exceeded` (429) errors into a `QuotaState` the UI shows; reaching quota stops hosted actions only, never local or LAN work, and never stops reporting.
Opt-in boundaries: only events for hosted (relay) sessions are reported; LAN/local usage is not sent; nothing is sent when logged out (events are discarded after a warning, not spooled forever).
scope_out: Computing token/minute counts locally: lane C029. Entitlement display: lane C064.
Opt-in product telemetry (separate contract and consent): lane C010.
`relay_bytes` and `queue_items` types: recorded by the relay side, so the client does not report them.
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed. The mock ingest endpoint validates the batch schema, enforces Idempotency-Key, dedupes by event id, applies the 60/min limit, can return 429/5xx on demand and emits `usage_warning`/`quota_reached` notices on its relay simulator.
interfaces: `new UsageReporter(o: { http: HttpClient; bus: EventBus; spoolDir: string; clock; ids: IdGenerator; isLoggedIn: () => boolean; flushIntervalMs?: number /*30000*/; maxBatch?: number /*500*/ })`; `start()`, `stop(): Promise<void>` (final flush, <= 5 s), `record(e: Omit<UsageEvent, 'id'>): void`, `flush(): Promise<{ sent: number; kept: number }>`
`UsageEvent = { id: string; type: 'agent_minutes'|'tokens_in'|'tokens_out'; qty: number; at: string; session_id?: string; agent_id?: string }` (qty non-negative integer)
`QuotaState = { level: 'ok'|'warning'|'reached'; pct?: number; resetsAt?: string }`; `quota(): QuotaState`; `onQuota(fn)`; `handleNotice(n: Notice): void`
acceptance: Recording 1 250 events then flushing produces 3 POSTs of 500, 500, 250 events; each body is <= 1 MiB; every POST has a distinct Idempotency-Key and the mock ingests 1 250 unique events.
A 502 on the first POST followed by 200 results in a second POST with the same key and same body, and the mock counts each event once (`Idempotency-Replayed: true` seen).
Killing the process after `record()` and before flush loses nothing: a new UsageReporter on the same spool sends the events once; a spool truncated mid-line recovers all complete lines.
Sustained recording at 1 000 events/s for 10 s keeps spool <= 10 000 events / 5 MiB (oldest dropped with a `dropped` counter exposed) and never blocks `record()` for > 5 ms (synchronous enqueue).
Requests are spaced to <= 60/min: flushing 200 000 spooled events (400 batches) takes >= 6 simulated minutes and never triggers a 429 from the mock.
A 429 `retry_after_s: 90` pauses all sending for 90 s (fake clock) while `record()` continues.
`usage_warning {pct:80}` sets `quota().level === 'warning'`; `quota_reached` sets `reached` and stays until `resets_at`; neither stops `flush()` nor any local command.
A 422 with `errors[].pointer` drops that batch, logs only the code and pointer, and continues with later batches.
Events without `session_id` of a hosted session (LAN/local) are never added to the spool; when logged out a single warning is logged and events are discarded.
`stop()` flushes within 5 s or leaves the spool intact for the next run.
tests: usage/batcher.test.ts: size/count limits, key stability, rate spacing on fake clock.
usage/spool.test.ts: crash recovery, truncation, caps, permissions 0600.
usage/quota.test.ts: notices to QuotaState transitions and reset.
usage/boundary.test.ts: LAN/local and logged-out events never reach the network.
usage/contract.test.ts: batches validate against the CT-API-USAGE request schema and fixtures.
guardrails: MUST send usage with an Idempotency-Key (required by CT-API-USAGE) and MUST reuse the same key and body when retrying; MUST NOT merge or re-split an unacknowledged batch.
MUST NOT include message text, prompts, paths, branch names, model names or any content in usage events; only the six documented fields.
MUST NEVER block, slow or fail an agent turn because usage reporting is failing; `record()` is synchronous and non-throwing.
MUST bound the spool (10 000 events / 5 MiB) and the in-memory queue; MUST NOT grow without limit when offline.
MUST NOT report LAN or local-only usage and MUST NOT treat reaching quota as a reason to stop local or LAN work.
MUST NOT use usage numbers for client-side enforcement decisions; the server is authoritative.
failure_modes: Server permanently rejects with 4xx (schema drift) -> batch dropped after logging code, reporter stays alive; a `poisoned` counter is exposed for diagnostics.
Clock set wrong -> `at` is the client time; the server tolerates skew only for tokens, so events are timestamped from the injected clock and never from the server in this lane.
Disk unwritable -> memory-only queue (cap 1 000 events) with a warning; events beyond the cap dropped oldest first.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the format of usage event `id` is not given in CT-IDS (no prefix listed); this card uses a plain 26-char ULID. The contract also does not say whether the client should report `queue_items`/`relay_bytes`; this card does not (the relay records those).
